subject: Integration: request/response design + auth choices for Pelotonix POC
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Samir Desai <samir@pelotonix.ai>, Tina Lopez <tina.lopez@pelotonix.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Oct 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps from today's integration call — SDK / auth / reranker

Hi Samir / Tina,

Thanks for taking the time earlier — quick recap and the things we need to keep the POC moving: 

TL;DR: Pelotonix is comfortable starting on Redwood Hosted (API) for the POC, wants deterministic answers for the user-facing workflow, and will provide a 10k-line sample dataset this week. Key asks below.

What we heard from Pelotonix on the call:
- Primary use case: customer support triage + answer retrieval into product UI (short answers, occasional tool calls).
- Volume: initial 30 QPS peak during load tests, target steady-state 8–12 QPS.
- Latency SLO: 200ms median preferred for short completions; streaming for UX would be ideal.
- Data sensitivity: PII in examples; SOC2 required eventually but not blocking for POC.

Decisions we need to confirm / asks for Pelotonix:
1) Auth & onboarding: you indicated hosted API is fine — do you want API keys or can you support mTLS? Also need an allowlist IP range if you choose server-to-server IP restriction.
2) Sample data: please share a representative sample (JSONL preferred) with labels for expected answers — you mentioned ~10k rows.
3) Retrieval & rerank approach: you said embeddings + reranker is acceptable; confirm whether latency or cost is the primary constraint.
4) UI behavior: do you want streaming token-by-token (for perceived responsiveness) or single final message for consistent deterministic output?

Proposed next steps:
- Pelotonix: send sample dataset + any security checklist items (SAML/SSO, IP restrictions) — Samir/Tina
- Redwood (Ben): prepare an SDK quickstart + minimal auth flow (API key + optional mTLS note)
- Redwood (Laura): draft a request/response schema (chat vs completions) and recommended top_k / rerank knobs

Attachment: pelotonix-poc-reqs.csv (fields we need for the sample dataset).

I'll hold a slot Tue 10–11 PT for a short technical sync if you want to go deeper.

Regards,

--
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0147

From: Samir Desai <samir@pelotonix.ai>

Cc: Tina Lopez <tina.lopez@pelotonix.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Oct 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps from today's integration call — SDK / auth / reranker

Thanks Soojin — quick answers inline.

- Auth: we prefer API keys for the POC (easier to rotate), but can do mTLS for later. No IP allowlist required for initial tests; we can revisit once we go to staging.
- Sample data: attaching data-sample.jsonl (sanitized) — should reflect the 10k-ish rows we discussed.
- Latency vs cost: latency is more important for the customer-facing UI; happy to accept slightly higher cost for the first phase.
- Streaming: yes, streaming would improve perceived responsiveness. If streaming adds non-determinism we need a fallback to a final deterministic response.

Two quick clarifications:
1) When you say "reranker" — do you mean a lightweight model we host (low-cost) or an LLM-based reranker? Latency trade-offs matter here.
2) For embeddings, what's your recommended dims / model for semantic recall at this scale (~10k docs)?

Attaching: data-sample.jsonl

Appreciate the quick follow-up. Tue 10–11 PT works for a deep tech sync.

Best,
Samir
Co-founder, Pelotonix
samir@pelotonix.ai

  - API key flow (rotate example)
  - Optional mTLS snippet and how the onboarding differs
  - A short note on recommended client-side token estimation (we should include a helper function; they asked about stop tokens behavior)

Ask 2 (Laura): propose a request/response schema for the POC and recommended flow:
  - Retrieval pipeline: embeddings model + index (suggest dims & model name), top_k for candidates, batching behavior for QPS
  - Reranker: lightweight classifier vs LLM reranker recommendation; expected latency per rerank and fallback policy (e.g., if reranker times out, use first-pass result)
  - Chat vs completions: recommend chat endpoint with tool-calling for product actions (structured JSON), and completions for short single-turn answers. Include example messages/payloads, max_tokens guidance (we have 2048 token budget for POC per call), and stop sequence handling.
  - Streaming semantics: recommend event schema for streaming deltas and a final "done" event with deterministic final text for auditing.

Constraints from Pelotonix: target 200ms median for short answers, streaming preferred, deterministic fallback required. We should also suggest quantization/latency knobs if they later request private/dedicated deployment.

Attachment: integration-checklist.md (minimal checklist for POC onboarding).

Can you both drop drafts into the shared Drive link by EOD? I will consolidate and send to Pelotonix ahead of Tue.

Thanks — Soojin

Subject: Re: Fwd: Recap & next steps from today's integration call — SDK / auth / reranker

Thanks — quick technical plan + sample snippets below.

1) Auth and SDK quickstart (attached: sdk-quickstart.patch)
- Recommend starting with API keys for POC. Provide rotating key recipe: short-lived key (7d) + server-side refresh token. Code snippet (JS) to attach a key and detect 401 and automatically refresh.

JS snippet (example):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-large", "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize invoice 123"}], "stream": false }'

2) Request/response schema recommendations
- Use Chat endpoint as primary: enables message history, tool-calling, and structured outputs. Completions OK for single-shot templated replies.
- Example response shape we propose (final): {"status": "ok", "output": {"type": "text"|"json", "content": "..."}, "tokens": {"prompt": 120, "completion": 56}} (we will surface as JSON in the API).
- max_tokens: suggest default max_tokens = 512 for UI short answers; allow override per-route. With a 2048 budget we can set guardrails and signal to UI when near budget.
- stop: support array of stop sequences; SDK helper to append safe stop markers for structured JSON outputs.

3) Tokenization and streaming semantics
- Client-side token estimation: provide a helper util that estimates tokens using the same tokenizer as the model. Recommend conservative +10% margin.
- Streaming: we will stream "delta" events with partial text and a final "done" event containing full tokens and deterministic final text for audit. Example stream events: 
  - event: {"type": "delta", "content": "The quick brown"}
  - event: {"type": "delta", "content": " fox jumps"}
  - event: {"type": "final", "content": "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog", "tokens": {...}}
- Stop behavior: if a stop sequence is detected, stream a final event that includes the trimmed final content and token counts.

4) Embeddings + rerank guidance
- Embeddings: recommend 1536-dim model (or smaller 1024 if cost is a concern). At ~10k docs, an ANN index with top_k=100 retrieval is reasonable. 
- Reranker: recommend a lightweight LLM reranker for top-20 candidates; if latency is critical, use a comparator classifier (logistic / tree) to do cheap filtering then run LLM rerank on the top 10.
- Fallback: if reranker exceeds 150ms, fall back to first-pass ordering and mark result as "best_effort" in API response.

Attachment: sdk-quickstart.patch
Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cPelotonixPOC (will add snippets).

I'll drop the code + examples into the Drive and the SDK repo by EOD; Laura, if you can sketch the proposed JSON schemas I'll merge them into a single doc to send to Pelotonix.
